title: Zuma's daughter remains a proud member and leader of the ANC
content:
Zuma's daughter remains a proud member and leader of the ANC
Newzroom Afrika
696000 subscribers
1559 likes
316498 views
15 Mar 2024
Imagine your father is a former President and your mother a senior cabinet executive, but now they stand on opposite sides of the political spectrum ahead of the May 29 Polls. This morning we speak to Thuthukile Zuma, the daughter of Jacob Zuma and Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma. In a recent X post, Thuthukile, who is a member of the ANC and its youth league posted “These are my parents. I am so proud to be born of these two human beings. I am also proud to be a member and leader of the ANC. Both are my realities and both will never change!”

She speaks to Aldrin Sampear.

Tune into Newzroom Afrika DStv channel 405 for more.

title: South Africa: Overcoming Apartheid
content: ANC leader and Deputy President of South Africa. His middle name was part of a sentence his father constructed – “Ngeke ngithule umuntu engigedla engihlekisa”, which means “I can’t keep quiet when someone pretends to love me with a deceitful smile.” The last part of the sentence was given to Zuma as a name, while the first part became the name of his brother, Ngekengithule. In 1977 he became a member of the ANC’s Executive Committee. In the 1980s he was a member of the ANC’s political and military council. A Zulu himself, he was seen as the ideal person to negotiate with the IFP and to get support for the ANC in Natal. In 1991, at the first ANC National Conference in South Africa after the organisation’s unbanning, Zuma was elected Deputy Secretary General of the ANC. At the same time he was elected National Chairperson of the ANC, and in 1997 he became the organisation’s Deputy President.

title: Jacob Zuma | Biography, Age, MK Party, ANC, Education ...
content: The president of South Africa, Jacob Zuma, speaking at the Sports for Peace Gala, Johannesburg, 2010. # Jacob Zuma. * When was Jacob Zuma the president of South Africa? **Jacob Zuma** (born April 12, 1942, Nkandla, South Africa) is a politician who served as president of South Africa from 2009 until he resigned under pressure in 2018. He also served as the country’s deputy president (1999–2005) and as deputy president (1997–2007) and president (2007–17) of the country’s ruling party, the African National Congress (ANC). In late 2023 he began to support a new political party, the uMkhonto weSizwe Party (commonly referred to as the MK Party), of which he became the president in April 2024. Although Zuma was widely expected to be chosen as the country’s next president in the 2009 election, he was not eligible to serve as interim president, who under the terms of the constitution had to be a member of the National Assembly.
